items.headline: Pirate Activity in the Gulf of Aden Escalates Amid Strait of Hormuz Disruption
items.teaser: Somali pirates have hijacked several commercial ships in recent months, taking advantage of the increased traffic off the eastern coast o…
items.story:
Somali pirates have hijacked several commercial ships in recent months, taking advantage of the increased traffic off the eastern coast of Africa caused by the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The hijackings, which include the oil tankers MT Honour 25, MT Eureka, and MT Asana, have occurred in the Gulf of Aden and off Puntland between April and July 2026, marking the largest attacks by Somali pirates in years. This surge in piracy has raised concerns among shipping companies and international authorities, who are now scrambling to respond to the growing threat. The sudden increase in traffic off the African coast has provided Somali pirates with a plethora of new targets, spread across thousands of miles of coastline.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for international oil trade, has forced hundreds of commercial ships to take longer routes around Africa, increasing the risk of pirate attacks. Somali piracy has a long history, with the first reported incidents dating back to the early 2000s, but the problem had largely been brought under control in recent years through international naval patrols and improved security measures. However, the current situation has created a perfect storm for pirate groups, who are now exploiting the increased traffic and lack of effective security measures in the region. The resurgence of Somali piracy has significant implications for global trade and security, as it threatens to disrupt the flow of oil and other critical commodities.

According to official reports, at least three oil tankers have been hijacked by Somali pirates in the past few months, with the most recent incident occurring in July 2026. The hijackings have been carried out by well-organized and heavily armed groups, who are using sophisticated tactics to evade detection and capture. International authorities have condemned the attacks and are working to coordinate a response to the growing threat. The United Nations and other international organizations have called for increased naval patrols and improved security measures to protect commercial ships in the region. Experts warn that the situation could escalate further if left unchecked, with potentially catastrophic consequences for global trade and security.

The surge in Somali piracy has sparked a range of reactions from stakeholders, with shipping companies and international authorities expressing concern and calling for action to address the problem. The International Maritime Organization has issued warnings to ships operating in the region, advising them to take extra precautions to avoid pirate attacks. Insurance companies are also taking a closer look at the situation, with some considering increases in premiums for ships operating in the affected areas. The public is also becoming increasingly aware of the issue, with many calling for greater international cooperation to combat the problem. As the situation continues to unfold, it is likely that we will see a range of responses from governments, international organizations, and other stakeholders.

The resurgence of Somali piracy has significant implications for regional and global security, as it threatens to destabilize the entire region and disrupt the flow of critical commodities. The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has already had a major impact on global oil markets, with prices rising sharply in recent months. The added threat of Somali piracy has the potential to exacerbate this situation, leading to further price increases and potential shortages. The international community is facing a complex challenge in responding to the situation, as it must balance the need to protect commercial ships and ensure the flow of critical commodities with the need to avoid escalating the situation and provoking further violence.

As the situation continues to evolve, it is likely that we will see a range of developments in the coming weeks and months. International authorities are expected to increase naval patrols and improve security measures in the region, while shipping companies and insurance providers will be closely monitoring the situation and adjusting their policies accordingly. The public will also be watching the situation closely, with many calling for greater international cooperation to combat the problem. Ultimately, the key to resolving the situation will be a coordinated and sustained effort from the international community, working together to address the root causes of the problem and ensure the safe passage of commercial ships through the region.

items.story:
Major technology companies, including Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, are falling short of their decarbonization goals, with some even moving in the opposite direction, despite initial pledges to reduce their carbon footprint. In 2019, Amazon committed to becoming carbon neutral by 2040, a decade ahead of the Paris climate agreement, while Google and Microsoft followed suit in 2020 with promises to become carbon-free by 2030. However, just six years later, these companies are struggling to meet their own targets, raising concerns about the tech industry's ability to mitigate its environmental impact. The shift away from decarbonization goals is particularly notable given the significant resources and expertise these companies possess. As the world's largest tech firms, their actions have far-reaching implications for the environment and the global effort to combat climate change.

The tech industry's initial enthusiasm for decarbonization was seen as a positive step towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating the effects of climate change. The Paris climate agreement, signed in 2015, aimed to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. By pledging to become carbon neutral or carbon-free, tech companies were seen as leaders in the private sector, setting an example for other industries to follow. However, the reality of meeting these targets has proven more challenging than expected, with companies facing numerous obstacles, including the complexity of their global supply chains and the difficulty of transitioning to renewable energy sources.

According to recent reports, Amazon's carbon emissions have actually increased in recent years, despite its pledge to become carbon neutral by 2040. Google and Microsoft have also faced challenges in meeting their decarbonization targets, with some critics arguing that their goals were overly ambitious from the start. Official statements from the companies acknowledge the difficulties they are facing, with Amazon citing the growth of its business and the complexity of its supply chain as major hurdles. Experts warn that the tech industry's failure to meet its decarbonization goals could have significant consequences, including damage to the companies' reputations and a loss of public trust.

The public and stakeholders are responding with growing concern to the tech industry's failure to meet its decarbonization targets. Environmental groups and activists have criticized the companies for their lack of progress, arguing that they are not doing enough to reduce their carbon footprint. Investors are also taking notice, with some expressing concerns about the long-term sustainability of the companies' business models. As the tech industry continues to grow and expand, its environmental impact is likely to come under increasing scrutiny, with companies facing pressure to demonstrate their commitment to reducing their carbon emissions and mitigating the effects of climate change.

The tech industry's struggles with decarbonization are part of a broader trend, with many companies and industries facing similar challenges in reducing their environmental impact. The transition to renewable energy sources and the adoption of sustainable practices are complex and often costly, requiring significant investments of time, money, and resources. However, the consequences of inaction are likely to be severe, with climate change posing a major threat to the global economy, public health, and the environment. As the world's largest tech firms, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have a critical role to play in leading the transition to a more sustainable future, and their failure to meet their decarbonization targets has significant implications for the global effort to combat climate change.

As the tech industry continues to grapple with the challenges of decarbonization, it remains to be seen whether companies will be able to get back on track and meet their targets. Upcoming decisions, such as the development of new sustainability strategies and the adoption of more aggressive decarbonization goals, will be closely watched by stakeholders and the public. The tech industry's ability to reduce its carbon footprint and mitigate the effects of climate change will depend on its willingness to invest in sustainable practices, adopt renewable energy sources, and prioritize the environment in its business decisions. With the clock ticking on the Paris climate agreement, the world will be watching to see if the tech industry can deliver on its promises and play a leadership role in the global effort to combat climate change.

items.story:
Europe's gas market is bracing for a potentially challenging winter, despite forecasts pointing to a strong El Niño event, which could bring milder temperatures to the region. The European winter of 2026-2027 is expected to be impacted by one of the most intense El Niño events since 2015, according to current predictions. However, analysts warn that only an exceptionally strong El Niño will have a meaningful impact on the region's liquefied natural gas (LNG) needs. European winter temperatures would need to be significantly above average for the region's LNG demand to decrease. This has raised concerns about the potential for gas shortages and price volatility in the coming months.

The El Niño phenomenon has a significant impact on global weather patterns, including European temperatures, and can influence the region's energy demand. Historically, strong El Niño events have led to milder winters in Europe, resulting in reduced demand for heating fuels like natural gas. However, the current energy landscape in Europe is complex, with the region still reeling from the aftermath of the Ukraine-Russia conflict and its impact on gas supplies. As a result, any potential relief from a strong El Niño event is being closely watched by market participants and policymakers.

According to Rystad Energy's analysis, European winter temperatures would need to be at least 2 degrees Celsius above the historical average for the region's LNG demand to fall to or below last winter's level. This is a significant threshold, and current forecasts suggest that such an outcome is unlikely. Forecasters currently rate the chances of an exceptionally strong El Niño event as a long shot, which has raised concerns about the potential for gas shortages and price volatility in the coming months. The European gas market is closely tied to global LNG markets, and any disruption to supplies or demand can have far-reaching implications.

The developments in the European gas market have significant implications for the global energy landscape. The region's energy demand has a ripple effect on global markets, and any disruption to supplies or demand can have far-reaching consequences. The current situation is also being watched closely by other regions, including Asia, which is a major consumer of LNG. As the winter of 2026-2027 approaches, market participants and policymakers will be closely watching the development of the El Niño event and its potential impact on European gas markets. With the European gas market still recovering from the aftermath of the Ukraine-Russia conflict, any relief from a strong El Niño event would be welcome, but it is unlikely to fully offset the underlying challenges facing the region's energy sector. items.story:
Israeli settlers have surrounded three Palestinian homes in the West Bank village of Qusra, cutting off essential services such as water and electricity, and trapping families inside for days. The siege has been ongoing, with security camera footage showing settlers erecting tents and attempting to break into the properties. Palestinian families living in the besieged homes have expressed deep concern for their safety, citing a constant sense of fear and anxiety. The situation has been exacerbated by the presence of Israeli forces, who have been filmed joining the settlers in the area.

The West Bank has been a focal point of tension between Israelis and Palestinians for decades, with issues of land ownership, settlement expansion, and access to resources being major points of contention. The village of Qusra, where the current siege is taking place, has experienced similar incidents in the past, with Palestinian residents facing challenges in maintaining control over their land and properties. The Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank has been widely criticized by the international community, with many viewing it as a major obstacle to achieving a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

According to eyewitness accounts and security footage, the settlers have been attempting to intimidate and harass the Palestinian families, making it difficult for them to access basic necessities such as food and medical care. The Israeli military has been accused of failing to intervene effectively to protect the Palestinian residents, with some footage showing soldiers standing by as settlers attempt to break into the homes. Official statements from the Israeli authorities have emphasized the need to maintain order and security in the area, but have not addressed the specific concerns of the Palestinian families.

The siege has had a profound impact on the daily lives of the Palestinian families, with children too afraid to leave their parents' side and adults struggling to cope with the constant stress and uncertainty. The lack of access to basic services such as water and electricity has also taken a toll on the health and well-being of the residents. The international community has expressed concern over the situation, with many calling for an immediate end to the siege and a return to negotiations aimed at resolving the underlying issues driving the conflict.

The situation in Qusra is part of a broader pattern of tension and conflict in the West Bank, where Israeli settlement expansion and Palestinian resistance have created a complex and volatile environment. The international community has long recognized the need for a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, but progress towards this goal has been slow and uneven. The current siege in Qusra has highlighted the need for renewed efforts to address the underlying issues driving the conflict, including the question of settlements and the rights of Palestinian residents.

As the situation in Qusra continues to unfold, attention will be focused on the response of the Israeli authorities and the international community to the crisis. The Palestinian families trapped in their homes will be waiting anxiously to see if their plight will be addressed, and if they will be able to return to a sense of normalcy and security. The incident has also raised questions about the role of the Israeli military in protecting Palestinian residents, and the need for greater accountability and transparency in the actions of Israeli forces in the West Bank.

Stripe, on the other hand, is a relatively new player in the sector, having been founded in 2010 by brothers Patrick and John Collison. According to reports, Stripe and Advent have bid $60.50 per share for PayPal, valuing the company at tens of billions of dollars. items.story:
Oracle's massive $165 billion data center project in New Mexico has hit a significant roadblock due to a delay in the construction of a natural gas pipeline, which is essential for powering the facility. The project, known as Project Jupiter, is slated to be built in Doña Ana County, and its schedule is now under threat. The data center project is one of the largest of its kind, and its development is being closely watched by the industry.

The data center is expected to create thousands of jobs and generate significant revenue for the local economy. However, the delay in the pipeline's construction has raised concerns about the project's viability and the potential impact on the local community.

According to regulatory filings, the expected in-service date for the Green Chile Project, the natural gas pipeline meant to power the data center, has been pushed back from August 15 to February 1, 2027. This six-month delay is attributed to various factors, including permitting issues and construction delays. Energy Transfer subsidiary Transwestern Pipeline, which is responsible for building the pipeline, has notified regulators of the revised timeline. The delay is expected to have a significant impact on Oracle's project schedule, with the company relying heavily on the pipeline to power its data center.

The delay in the pipeline's construction has sparked concerns among stakeholders, including local residents and business leaders. Oracle has not commented publicly on the delay, but industry experts say that the company will need to reassess its project schedule and explore alternative options for powering the data center. The delay in the pipeline's construction is not an isolated incident, with several other data center projects across the United States facing similar challenges. The demand for data centers is on the rise, driven by the growing need for cloud computing and data storage. However, the construction of these facilities is often hindered by regulatory issues, environmental concerns, and infrastructure challenges. The Oracle project is a prime example of the complexities involved in building large-scale data centers, and its outcome will be closely watched by the industry.

As the project moves forward, Oracle will need to navigate the complexities of the delay and find alternative solutions to power its data center. The company will also need to work closely with regulators and local stakeholders to ensure that the project is completed on time and within budget. The outcome of the project will have significant implications for the local economy and the data center industry as a whole. With the revised timeline for the pipeline's construction, all eyes will be on Oracle to see how the company responds to the delay and whether it can still deliver on its ambitious plans for the Project Jupiter data center.

The ban is expected to remain in place until further notice, and its implementation will be closely monitored by relevant authorities. Authorities have warned that the use of single-use grills can spark devastating fires, especially in areas with dry vegetation.

The use of disposable barbecues has been a longstanding issue, with many experts and environmentalists raising concerns about their safety and environmental impact. In recent years, there have been numerous instances of wildfires caused by careless disposal of barbecues, highlighting the need for stricter regulations. The current heatwave and drought conditions have exacerbated the situation, making it essential for the government to take proactive measures to prevent such incidents. Experts have welcomed the ban, stating that it is a necessary step to protect the public and the environment. The ban on disposable barbecues is expected to have a significant impact on the public, particularly during the summer months when outdoor gatherings and barbecues are common. As the situation continues to evolve, it is likely that there will be further reactions and responses from various stakeholders.

The temporary ban on disposable barbecues is part of a broader effort to address the growing threat of wildfires, which is a global concern. Many countries are experiencing similar conditions, and there is a growing recognition of the need for international cooperation to address this issue. The use of disposable barbecues is just one aspect of a larger problem, and the government's decision is seen as a step in the right direction. Regional authorities are also taking measures to prevent wildfires, including implementing burn bans and increasing surveillance in high-risk areas. The international community is watching the situation closely, and it is likely that other countries will follow suit in implementing similar measures.

As the situation continues to unfold, the government will be closely monitoring the effectiveness of the ban and assessing the need for further measures to prevent wildfires. The public is being urged to remain vigilant and to take necessary precautions to prevent fires, including properly disposing of cigarettes and other flammable materials. items.story:
A woman has been cleared of owning a dog that fatally bit a man, resulting in his death from severe blood loss. Chanel Fong was accused of being the owner of the XL bully that bit her partner's father, Keven Jones, on the leg. The incident occurred when Jones was visiting Fong and her partner, and the dog's bite led to significant blood loss, which ultimately caused his death. The investigation into the incident has been ongoing, with authorities working to determine the circumstances surrounding the fatal bite.

The case has drawn attention to the issue of dog ownership and the potential dangers associated with certain breeds. XL bullies are a type of dog that is often considered to be a high-risk breed due to their size and strength. In recent years, there have been several incidents involving XL bullies and other similar breeds, resulting in serious injuries and fatalities. As a result, many jurisdictions have implemented laws and regulations aimed at restricting the ownership of these breeds or requiring special licenses and insurance for their owners.

According to official statements, Fong has been cleared of any wrongdoing in connection with the incident, as it was determined that she was not the owner of the dog at the time of the bite. The actual owner of the dog has not been publicly identified, and it is unclear whether any charges will be filed in connection with the incident. Experts have noted that dog bites can be unpredictable and may occur even when the dog is well-cared for and properly trained. In this case, the investigation found that the dog's bite was an isolated incident and not the result of any negligence on the part of Fong or her partner.

The outcome of the investigation has been met with mixed reactions from the public, with some expressing relief that Fong has been cleared of any wrongdoing and others calling for stricter regulations on dog ownership. Jones's family has declined to comment on the matter, citing their ongoing grief and shock over his death. The incident has also sparked a wider debate about the need for increased awareness and education about dog safety and the importance of responsible pet ownership. Many animal welfare organizations have weighed in on the issue, emphasizing the need for owners to take steps to prevent dog bites and ensure the safety of both people and animals.

The incident has also raised questions about the effectiveness of current laws and regulations regarding dog ownership, particularly with regards to high-risk breeds like XL bullies. Some advocates have called for stricter laws and increased penalties for owners who fail to properly care for and control their dogs. Others have argued that education and awareness campaigns are more effective in preventing dog bites and promoting responsible pet ownership. As the debate continues, authorities are likely to face increased pressure to review and revise existing laws and regulations to ensure public safety.

As the case comes to a close, attention is likely to turn to the issue of preventing similar incidents in the future. Experts are expected to continue studying the circumstances surrounding the fatal bite, with a focus on identifying potential risk factors and developing strategies for mitigating those risks. Meanwhile, Fong and her partner are likely to face an ongoing process of healing and recovery, both from the loss of Jones and from the trauma of the incident itself. items.headline: Tech Giant Suggests New Revenue Model Involving 15% Commission on External Transactions
items.teaser: Apple is seeking permission from a federal judge to impose a commission of up to 15% on purchases made through external links in iOS apps…
items.story:
Apple is seeking permission from a federal judge to impose a commission of up to 15% on purchases made through external links in iOS apps, a move that could significantly impact the way developers earn revenue from their apps. This proposal is part of an ongoing legal battle between Apple and app developers, with the tech giant arguing that it is entitled to a cut of all transactions facilitated by its platform. The request was made in a federal court filing, as Apple attempts to clarify its rights and obligations under its App Store agreements. The company's proposal has sparked intense interest and debate within the tech industry, with many developers and observers waiting to see how the court will rule on the matter.

The dispute over Apple's commission rates and App Store policies has been simmering for several years, with many developers complaining that the company's 30% cut of in-app purchases is excessive and stifles innovation. In response to these criticisms, Apple has made some concessions, such as reducing its commission rate to 15% for smaller developers and allowing certain types of apps to circumvent its in-app purchase system. However, the company has also taken steps to enforce its App Store guidelines and prevent developers from using external payment links to avoid its commissions. This latest proposal is seen as an attempt by Apple to establish a clear and consistent policy on external purchases and to ensure that it can continue to generate revenue from its platform.

According to Apple's court filing, the proposed 15% commission rate would apply to all purchases made through external links in iOS apps, regardless of whether the transaction is processed through Apple's in-app purchase system or a third-party payment provider. The company argues that this rate is necessary to compensate it for the costs and risks associated with facilitating transactions on its platform, including the need to maintain secure payment processing systems and protect users from fraud. Apple also points out that its commission rates are comparable to those charged by other platform holders, such as Google and Amazon, and that they are necessary to support the continued development and maintenance of its ecosystem.

The reaction to Apple's proposal has been mixed, with some developers and industry observers expressing concern that the company's commission rates are too high and will stifle innovation and competition. Others have argued that Apple's proposal is reasonable and necessary to ensure that the company can continue to invest in its platform and provide a secure and convenient experience for users. The proposal has also sparked debate among lawmakers and regulators, who are increasingly scrutinizing the business practices of large tech companies and considering new rules and regulations to promote competition and protect consumers.

The outcome of Apple's proposal could have significant implications for the broader tech industry, as other platform holders and developers watch to see how the court rules on the matter. If Apple is successful in imposing a 15% commission rate on external purchases, it could set a precedent for other companies to follow, potentially leading to a more standardized and consistent approach to platform fees and commissions. On the other hand, if the court rejects Apple's proposal, it could embolden developers and other stakeholders to push for more favorable terms and greater flexibility in their dealings with platform holders.

As the court considers Apple's proposal, the company and its stakeholders are awaiting a decision that could have far-reaching consequences for the future of the App Store and the broader tech industry. The ruling could also have implications for ongoing antitrust investigations and lawsuits targeting Apple and other large tech companies, as regulators and lawmakers seek to promote greater competition and innovation in the digital economy. With the outcome of the case still uncertain, developers and industry observers are watching closely to see how the court will balance the competing interests of Apple, its developers, and its users, and what the ultimate impact will be on the company's platform and business model.

items.story: ദേശീയപാതയോരത്ത് വീട്, വാണിജ്യസ്ഥാപന നിർമാണത്തിനുള്ള പുതുക്കിയ ദൂരപരിധി; തീരദേശമേഖലയ്ക്ക് തിരിച്ചടി Mathrubhumiദേശീയപാതയോര നിയന്ത്രണം: നാടിന്റെ വികസനവും ജനങ്ങളുടെ ഉപജീവനവും മുടങ്ങും: സുപ്രിം കോടതി ഉത്തരവിനെതിരെ ദേശീയപാത സംരക്ഷണ സമിതി Suprabhaathamദേശീയ പാതയോരത്ത് നിർമ്മാണം കടുകട്ടി, സുപ്രീംകോടതി ഉത്തരവ് നടപ്പിലാക്കാൻ കേരളം Kerala Kaumudiദേശീയപാതയോട് ചേര്‍ന്ന് വീടും കടകളും വേണ്ട..! ആശങ്കയേറ്റി സുപ്രീംകോടതി ഉത്തരവ് Oneindia Malayalamദേശീയപാതയോരത്ത് വീടിന് 40 മീറ്റർ, കച്ചവടത്തിന് 75 മീറ്റർ ദൂരപരിധി;

items.story: റേഷൻ അരിയിൽ 'ഓണത്തല്ല്; കൊമ്പുകോർത്ത് അനൂപ് ജേക്കബും ജി.ആർ. അനിലും Mathrubhumiഓണം അരി സ്പെഷലാണ്, കുക്കറിൽ വേവിച്ചേക്കല്ലേ; വെന്തു കുഴയും Manorama Onlineഓണ റേഷന്‍: പിങ്ക് കാർഡിന് 5 കിലോ സ്പെഷ്യൽ അരി ഇല്ല; പകരം 3 കിലോ OMSS അരി 26 രൂപയ്ക്ക്; നീല, വെള്ള, തവിട്ട് കാര്‍ഡുകളിലും മാറ്റം Samayam Malayalamസംസ്ഥാന സർക്കാരിന്‍റെ ഓണക്കിറ്റ് വിതരണം ആരംഭിച്ചെന്ന് മന്ത്രി അനൂപ് ജേക്കബ് Asianet News Malayalamറേഷന്‍ അരിയുടെ വില വര്‍ധിപ്പിച്ചിട്ടില്ല, മറിച്ചുള്ള പ്രചരണങ്ങള്‍ വ്യാജം; ഭക്ഷ്യ വകുപ്പ് Siraj Daily

items.story: കര്‍ണാടകയില്‍ വനിതാ സബ് ഇന്‍സ്‌പെക്ടറെ ബി.ജെ.പി എം.എല്‍.എയുടെ മകള്‍ മര്‍ദിച്ചതായി പരാതി Suprabhaathamക്ഷേത്രത്തിൽ പ്രവേശനം അനുവദിക്കാൻ വൈകി; പൊലീസ് ഉദ്യോഗസ്ഥയെ മർദിച്ച് ബിജെപി എംഎൽഎയുടെ മകൾ Manorama Onlineവനിതാ പൊലീസുദ്യോഗസ്ഥയെ കരണത്തടിച്ചെന്ന് പരാതി, ബിജെപി എംഎൽഎയുടെ മകൾക്കെതിരെ കേസ് Kerala Kaumudiവനിതാ പോലീസ് ഉദ്യോഗസ്ഥയെ മർദ്ദിച്ച് ബിജെപി നേതാവിന്റെ മകൾ; മാപ്പു പറഞ്ഞ് എംഎൽഎ, കേസെടുത്തു Mathrubhumiകർണാടകയിൽ ബിജെപിനേതാവിന്റെ മകൾ വനിതാ പോലീസ് ഉദ്യോഗസ്ഥയെ മർദ്ദിച്ചതായി ആരോപണം,കേസെടുത്തു Karma News

items.headline: Immune cells flood into the aging brain, Stanford scientists discover
items.teaser: Scientists have discovered that the aging human brain may be far less isolated from the rest of the body than once believed. Stanford res…
items.story: Scientists have discovered that the aging human brain may be far less isolated from the rest of the body than once believed. Stanford researchers found that large numbers of immune cells from the blood begin entering the brain as early as middle age, where they can transform into microglia, the brain’s specialized immune cells. The finding overturns a long-standing assumption that these cells remain largely separate from the body’s immune system throughout life.

items.headline: Scientists detect a nuclear reactor’s ghostly afterglow for the first time
items.teaser: Nuclear reactors may go dark, but their fuel continues producing a faint antineutrino “glow” long after shutdown. Researchers have now de…
items.story: Nuclear reactors may go dark, but their fuel continues producing a faint antineutrino “glow” long after shutdown. Researchers have now detected that residual signal for the first time, finding it closely matched predictions of radioactive decay inside the reactor and nearby spent-fuel pools. The breakthrough suggests antineutrino detectors could eventually monitor reactors even when they are offline.

items.headline: A stress hormone may help the brain repair itself
items.teaser: A surprising stress-related signal may help the brain repair itself after injury. Researchers found that myelin-producing precursor cells…
items.story: A surprising stress-related signal may help the brain repair itself after injury. Researchers found that myelin-producing precursor cells rapidly release the stress hormone CRH near damaged brain tissue, helping control how those cells mature and rebuild protective nerve insulation. The same system also influences brain development and the thickness of myelin later in life. The findings could offer new clues about how early-life stress contributes to psychiatric disorders.

items.headline: Women taking estrogen had fewer signs of Alzheimer’s in their brains
items.teaser: Women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life were less likely to develop dementia and showed fewer signs of Alzheimer’s dis…
items.story: Women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life were less likely to develop dementia and showed fewer signs of Alzheimer’s disease in their brains, according to a large study of more than 21,000 participants. Hormone therapy use was linked to 39% lower odds of a dementia diagnosis and 35% lower odds of Alzheimer’s-related brain changes at autopsy, including amyloid plaques and tau tangles. Biomarker tests also suggested less amyloid buildup among hormone therapy users.

items.story: JWST has uncovered surprising clues that Neptune’s strange inner moons may be the wreckage of an ancient cosmic catastrophe. Researchers detected clay-like minerals on Larissa, Galatea, and Neptune’s rings that form in the presence of liquid water—yet the moons themselves show no obvious water ice. The material likely came from deep inside much larger icy moons that were shattered when Triton was captured by Neptune, destroying much of the planet’s original satellite system.
